ai.title: Move enableMapSet from init-app to per-store immer imports
ai.summary: CLI state stores now call `enableMapSet()` at module scope instead of relying on a global init in `init-app.ts`. Root cause: immer's Map/Set support is process-global, so centralizing it in init made direct store imports throw `[Immer] minified error nr: 0` and tests pass only by import-order luck. Scope: `chat-store.ts`, `feedback-store.ts`, `message-block-store.ts`, `publish-store.ts`, and `init-app.ts`. `enableMapSet()` is idempotent, so per-store calls are safe and make each store self-contained on import.

eli5.text: The CLI's chat, feedback, message block, and publish state stores now enable immer's Map/Set support themselves at module load, instead of relying on a single global call during app initialization. If you imported any of these stores directly (e.g. in a test or tooling context) before the app had fully bootstrapped, immer's plugin hadn't been activated yet, so the store would throw [Immer] minified error nr: 0 and only worked when another file happened to run first and enable the plugin. Enabling it per-store makes each store correct on its own import, and makes a store that forgets fail consistently everywhere instead of only outside the app.

ai.summary: Added five analytics event enums in common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts covering Web creation gate redirects, first-session onboarding steps/completion, and workspace spotlight tour steps/completion. These track user drop-off and funnel completion across Web surfaces. Gate redirects pair with Convex web_gate_decision rows to separate 'did redirect land?' (PostHog) from 'which ideas?' (Convex). Onboarding and tour events capture per-step answered/skipped states and final completion metrics.

eli5.text: When you build your first project on Freebuff's web version, the team is now tracking how you move through two key moments: the short onboarding questions that appear while your first build runs, and the guided tour of your new workspace afterward. If the system decides your idea is better suited for the desktop or CLI tool, it also records when you click through to that alternative, so it can tell whether you actually landed there. Nothing you see changes visually yet, this simply adds the tracking needed to measure where people drop off, so the team can later find out which step (onboarding question, tour pane, or gate redirect) is most often left unfinished.

ai.title: Isolate integration tests in CLI, common, agent-runtime, SDK test
ai.summary: Default `test` scripts in `cli`, `common`, `packages/agent-runtime`, and `sdk` now explicitly exclude `*.integration.test.ts` and `*.integration.test.tsx` files via new `test:files` helper scripts. This change prevents integration tests from running during standard unit test executions, separating them into dedicated `test:files:integration` targets. The mechanism relies on `find` commands within package.json scripts to filter file patterns before passing them to `bun test`. This applies to the CLI, Common, Agent Runtime, and SDK packages.

eli5.text: When developers run the project's test suite, it now only runs everyday unit tests and skips longer-running integration tests by default. Those integration tests are filtered into separate commands, so a developer choosing to run the full test suite would notice that certain tests no longer run unless they explicitly select the integration test option. This makes routine testing faster and keeps different kinds of tests organized. The change is live today and affects how tests are grouped across several parts of the project.

ai.title: launcher-disconnect test drains output on exit
ai.summary: Updated `launcher-disconnect.test.ts` to resolve on `child.once('exit')` rather than `close`, adding a `OUTPUT_DRAIN_MS` (750ms) timer to capture stdout/stderr. This prevents test hangs when grandchild processes inherit stdio and keep pipes open, ensuring the fixture's exit code and diagnostic output are captured before the 15s timeout. Scope limited to CLI test infrastructure; no shipped code changes.

eli5.text: When the CLI's package launcher disappears during a test, the test now waits for the process to fully exit and gives it a short window to finish sending any remaining output before declaring success or failure. This only affects the test infrastructure that verifies the CLI exits cleanly when its launcher vanishes, preventing the test from hanging and throwing away the fixture's exit code and diagnostic messages. A surviving CLI still causes the test to fail rather than pass, and the fix is live in the test suite today.

ai.title: Clamp terminal timeoutseconds to 600s in basher agent
ai.summary: Added `clampTerminalTimeoutSeconds` to `run-terminal-command.ts` to enforce a 600-second maximum on model-supplied `timeout_seconds`, preserving the `-1` sentinel and defaulting to 30 for invalid values. Updated `basher.ts` schema descriptions to warn against over-long budgets and document the clamp. This prevents models from setting excessively long timeouts (e.g., 50 minutes) for fast commands, which previously caused users to wait through hangs without intervention. The change applies to synchronous commands; `-1` and `process_type: BACKGROUND` remain unaffected for open-ended tasks.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs a command in your terminal, it used to be able to tell it to wait up to 50 minutes even for quick actions. If something hung, you could end up sitting through that entire wait with nothing happening. The assistant now has a hard upper limit on how long it can set that wait for regular commands, so a stuck command stops on its own instead of leaving you staring at a frozen screen. Anything that genuinely needs more time still has its own way to run in the background or wait with no timeout.
